title: Russia launches wave of missile strikes on Ukrainian cities and energy infrastructure
body:
On 10 October 2022, Russia struck cities across Ukraine with missiles, including Kyiv for the first time since 26 June. Missiles also hit 14 other regions, among them Dnipropetrovsk, Lviv, Ternopil, Khmelnytskyi, Zhytomyr, Sumy, Kharkiv and Odesa. The strikes began what became a sustained Russian campaign against Ukrainian energy infrastructure.

According to figures compiled by the Ukraine Crisis Media Center, 11 people had been killed by 4 p.m., five of them in central Kyiv, and between 87 and 90 people were wounded. About 70 sites were damaged, including 29 critical infrastructure sites, and the strikes caused 30 fires. Four regions, Lviv, Poltava, Sumy and Ternopil, lost power completely, and others had partial outages and some lost water and internet service.

Energy Minister Herman Halushchenko said Russia was destroying Ukraine's energy system. Ukraine's Ministry of Energy announced that electricity exports would be suspended from 11 October. Putin later described the October missile strikes as retaliation for the Crimean Bridge explosion of 8 October. Later waves followed, including on 22 October, when nearly 1.5 million households lost electricity, and Zelensky said 30 percent of power stations had been destroyed since 10 October.
